---
title: "Top 2000 CG Sites Excel Export"
---

```{r}
#| label: load-packages
#| echo: false

pacman::p_load(openxlsx2, install = FALSE)

# Source the optimized function for adding CG data to Excel
source(here("custom_func/add_cg_to_excel_function.R"))
```

## Introduction

This document prepares an Excel file containing the top 2000 CG sites for each dementia category (demcat). Each demcat's data will be placed in a separate sheet with appropriate formatting.

## Load Data

```{r}
#| label: load-data

# Source for the per-category top CpG lists
source(here("custom_func/select_top_cg.R"))
annot <- read_rds(here("data/upon_request/annotated_asso_wide.rds"))

# List of demcats
demcats <- c("normal2mci", "stable_mci", "normal2incid", "mci2incid", "prev")

# Derive the top 2000 CG sites for each demcat
top2000_data <- demcats |>
  set_names() |>
  map(~ select_top_cg(annot, .x, 2000)) |>
  imap(~{
    .x |>
      arrange(desc(.data[[glue("nlog10_p_value_{.y}")]])) |>
      mutate(rank = row_number(), .before = 1)
  })

# Check the structure of the first dataset
glimpse(top2000_data[[1]])
```

## Create Excel Workbook

```{r}
#| label: create-excel

# Start timing
tic("Excel creation")

# Create a workbook
wb <- wb_workbook() |>
  wb_set_bookview(window_height = 100000L, window_width = 100000L)

# Add each demcat's data to a separate sheet
suppl_data_order <- 2
for (dc in demcats) {
  # Create legend for the sheet
  # The comparison, effect-size, group and follow-up sentences are those of the
  # Data S1 legend (01_DMP403_cg_excel.qmd); change both together.
  cg_legend <- glue("Data S{suppl_data_order}. Top 2000 CpG sites for the {dc} group, decreasingly ranked by significance (−log10 P) in this group. Each group was compared with the stable normal reference group in a linear regression adjusted for age, sex, smoking status and white blood cell proportions. Effect size is ΔM, the covariate-adjusted difference in mean M-value between the group and the stable normal group. Groups: normal2mci, cognitively normal at baseline and mild cognitive impairment (MCI) about 5 years later, with no dementia during follow-up; stable_mci, MCI at baseline and no dementia during follow-up; normal2incid, cognitively normal at baseline and dementia diagnosed during follow-up; mci2incid, MCI at baseline and dementia diagnosed during follow-up; prev, dementia already present at baseline (blood draw). Follow-up lasted up to 13.4 years. The GREAT-annotated genes were used to explore the Gene Ontology (GO) enrichment for the top 1000 (rank 1 through 1000) and top 2000 (rank 1 through 2000) CpGs.") |>
    as.character()
  suppl_data_order <- suppl_data_order + 1

  # Add the sheet with data
  wb <- wb |> 
    add_cg_to_excel(
      df = top2000_data[[dc]], 
      sheet_name = glue("CG_{dc}"), 
      legend = cg_legend
    )
  
  # Print progress
  cat(glue("Added sheet for {dc} \n"))
}

# Save the workbook
fs::dir_create(here("extended_data/output"))
output_file <- here("extended_data/output/top2000_cg_sites.xlsx")
wb |> wb_save(output_file)

# End timing
toc()

cat(glue("Excel file saved to: {output_file}\n"))
```

## Summary

This document has created an Excel workbook with five sheets, one for each dementia category:
1. prev - Prevalent dementia
2. normal2mci - Normal to Mild Cognitive Impairment
3. stable_mci - Stable Mild Cognitive Impairment
4. normal2incid - Normal to Incident dementia
5. mci2incid - Mild Cognitive Impairment to Incident dementia

Each sheet contains the top 2000 CG sites for that category, formatted according to the specifications in the `add_cg_to_excel` function.
